name: De Vinne 18pt 1897
designer: Unidentified in the retained source pages
foundry: Shown by the United States Government Printing Office; 1897 stock mark Keystone–10
description: Eighteen-point De Vinne with flared serifs, broad W, sweeping Q and R tails, double-storey a and g, and mixed-height default figures. Optional lining figures, descending three and four, and a tall zero preserve additional observed forms.
character_set_notes: Complete observed A–Z, a–z and ten figures; period, comma, colon, semicolon, question mark, right apostrophe and double-bar historical hyphen encoded as hyphen-minus; nine whole diagonal fractions, cent and percent. Space advance, sidebearings and fraction vertical placement are modern layout choices. No unsupported punctuation or aliases are inferred.
observed: The 1897 specimen supplies both complete eighteen-point alphabets and a figure 2. Matching eighteen-point census and job-room impressions supply clearer selected letters, figures and punctuation. The census sets lowercase j before i; the recorded selections follow their actual shapes. The 1904 poster and figure page supply four punctuation characters and a lining set. Existing 3, 4, 6 and 8 serve both figure settings. The intact GPO tall zero supersedes the softer matching Handy impression; the short job-room zero remains the default. Matching ATF fraction assortments provide nine whole diagonal fractions, cent and percent; intact New York, Handy and BYU impressions are selected at one physical scale per source page. The NYPL 1898 Desk Book shows descending 3 and 4 beside text at the same optical size; whole impressions supply optional oldstyle forms.
reconstructed: No visible glyphs are invented. Uniform source-page scaling, measured rigid baseline rotation, local paper correction and modern spacing prepare observed forms. No cross-size substitution. Recorded one-, two- and four-pixel enclosed printing pinholes in L, 9 and comma are cleaned without changing their outside contours or intended counters. Fraction row-center placement is a modern layout convention; the source charts do not establish a historical text baseline.

revival.notes: Complete observed alphabets, figures, punctuation and fraction companions; eight unencoded figure alternatives. lnum supplies lining forms, onum and ss02 select descending 3/4, and ss01 selects tall zero. Ten retained native pages document the sources. Fraction row centers use declared modern placement; descending 3/4 use an observed text baseline.
